text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141. @
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet decided yesterday to cut 7.9 billion forints from the 1997 budget in order to offset the excessive social insurance deficit. Prime Minister's spokesman Elemer Kiss said the cabinet continues to bar foreigners from obtaining land property. The cabinet approved an amendment to the act on bankruptcy and winding-up procedures in an effort to prevent abuses and speed up procedures. @
- The parliamentary commission set up to investigate the case of the 804 million forints paid to lawyer Marta Tocsik by the State Privatisation and Holding Rt (APV) met for the first time yesterday.

- The recently established Central Crime-Fighting Directorate has secured 500 million forints of the 804 million paid to Marta Tocsik after conducting house searches in three office buildings of the Budapest headquarters of APV.
- Free Democrat President Ivan Peto said next month's party convention will examine whether secession or staying in the coalition is the appropriate solution. @

- Consultants in the privatisation of the national telecoms firm Matav were paid disproportionately high fees and the interests of the state were not always given appropriate consideration, said State Audit Office director Arpad Koves.
- The directors of EBRD confirmed its strategy for Hungary.
- Economic growth will only occur if the decline in private consumption stops, concludes the latest analysis by economic researchers Kopint-Datorg. @

- Effective immediately, Vektor Broker Rt is banned from accepting any new commissions or from conducting transactions on its account at the stock exchange and may not engage in security trading outside the exchange until December 31.

- Researchers exploring US archives have found traces of a secret agreement concluded between Switzerland and the Hungarian, Czech and Polish governments, according to which Swiss nationals received Jewish assets deposited in Swiss banks as compensation for their assets nationalised in the three countries. @
NEPSZABADSAG
- President Arpad Goncz unveiled statue of Hungarian composer Bela Bartok in Ankara.
- Six firms from five countries have submitted bids in the second round of a tender called by the Defence Ministry for the purchase of anti-aircraft rockets for 20 billion forints.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Minister of Culture Balint Magyar and his French counterpart Thursday agreed in Paris that a Hungarian cultural year will be observed in France in 2001. @
- Household savings rose 18.9 billion forints in September, well below the year's monthly average of over 40 billion forints, reports the National Bank of Hungary.
- Austrian bank Creditanstalt and ABN-Amro of the Netherlands submitted bids for Magyar Hitel Bank Rt. yesterday.
- The securities firm of Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank will begin selling German bonds issued by the bank's majority owner, Bayerische Landesbank.
- Border guard officials announced that traffic restriction will be introduced from 7 a.m. Friday to 7 p.m. due to reconstruction. @
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Belgian hotel firm City Hotels is accusing Danubius Hotels of aiming for an illegal dominance of the market of Hungarian quality hotels.
